text:
sang: quick dump from today's profiler — p95 is largely prefill for short prompts but p99 is dominated by decode for long streams. looks like kernel-switch and kv-miss correlation spiking at tail.

marta: can you paste the numbers? curious about absolute ms and token counts.

sang: sure, snippet from perf-runner: \n```\nmodel: redwood-open-7b\nprefill: p50 12ms p95 48ms p99 120ms\ndecode:  p50 8ms  p95 60ms p99 260ms\nkv-miss spikes coincide with decode p99 (>200ms)\nmicrobatch-size=8 -> best throughput but 2x p99 vs size=2\n```\n
jon: so microbatching helps throughput but amplifies tail via kv thrash. is the kernel switch on token-length threshold or on batch occupancy?

sang: current switch: if batch_tokens > 1024 we pick big-matmul kernel; else small-kernel. but occupancy + kv-miss pattern matters. with big batches we see cold KV lookups causing stalls during decode.

lee: thought: separate kernels per phase. prefill uses kernel A (batched, fused attention), decode uses low-latency kernel B with better single-token throughput. that way decode doesn't wait for big-batch optimized paths.

marta: we already have a prefill/decode kernel selection flag but it's heuristic-only. proposal: add phase-aware kernel hint from scheduler and a microbatch-adaptive cap — e.g. cap decode microbatch to 4 while allowing prefill to burst to 12.

jon: how about KV warmup: if request likely to decode long tail, pre-warm KV for top-k prefixes from cache? maybe cheap async warming during prefill for predicted next-token keys.

sang: agree. experiment plan: \n1) enforce decode microbatch max=4 and prefer low-latency kernel.\n2) async KV warmup for top-3 prefix candidates during prefill.\n3) instrument per-token stall reasons (kernel wait vs kv-io vs cuda-sync).

lee: add an A/B canary on a subset of traffic (10%) and compare p95/p99 + tokens/sec. also measure cost delta.

infra-bot: canary cluster provisioned: canary-rl-7b-02 ready in us-west.

marta: i ran a quick sim: reducing decode batch cap to 4 drops p99 decode from 260ms -> 150ms on avg, but throughput drops ~12%. seems promising.

jon: we should surface a routing policy: route latency-sensitive customers to decode-capped nodes, and throughput customers to bulk nodes. that keeps SLOs intact while preserving overall utilization.

sang: agreed. next steps: I will add metrics for per-token stall tags + implement decode microbatch cap toggle. jon, can you prototype async kv warmup sketch? lee, set up canary traffic split and dashboards (p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, kv-hit-rate).

lee: on it. dashboard tiles i'll create: decode_tail_reasons, kv_hit_rate_by_prefix_len, kernel_switch_count.

jon: prototype ETA EOD tomorrow. i'll drop a follow-up with microbench numbers.

marta: i'll prepare a short runbook for ops: when to flip back if canary worsens cost or error rates. include rollback on 2x p99 regression.

sang: awesome. tagging @eng-sre for visibility. anything else?

lee: maybe one more: log a small sample of raw CUDA queues for worst 1% to inspect kernel stalls. that helped last time.

sang: good call. adding to infra checklist. thanks all :thumbsup:
